source.publication: 2025 DR 0104 Booklet (Colorado Individual Income Tax), DR 0104 and DR 0104AD
source.section: DR 0104AD line 7 / line 8 Military Retirement Subtraction (PDF p.20 Lines 7-8; DR 0104AD p.2 lines 7-8 '(under age 55)'); DR 0104 lines 1, 10-13 (PDF p.8, p.10); tax table PDF p.34-35

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 60,000.00 + military pension paid by the federal government (you) 12,000.00 = 72,000.00. Federal taxable income = 72,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 56,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). DR 0104 line 1 federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15) 56,250.00; lines 2-9 additions 0.00 (no state income tax addback, no other-state bond interest; federal AGI 72,000.00 is not over 300,000, so no line 4 deduction addback); line 10 subtotal 56,250.00. DR 0104AD: Line 7 (primary taxpayer, age 48, 54 or younger): smaller of taxable military retirement 12,000.00 and 15,000.00 = 12,000.00. Line 22 subtotal = 12,000.00; DR 0104 line 11 = 12,000.00. Line 12 Colorado taxable income = 56,250.00 - 12,000.00 = 44,250.00. Line 13 tax = 4.4% x 44,250.00 = 1,947.00 (the tax table row over 44,200.00 but not over 44,300.00, PDF p.35, gives 1,947.00; expected keeps the formula figure). No credits claimed: 0.00. Colorado income tax 1,947.00.
accepted_approximations: Tax is figured on the exact income at 4.4%; below 50,000 the booklet uses the tax table, which taxes each 100-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds to the dollar.
